headline: $6,000 sale of Rock Road lots approved; zoning commission asked to speed up data center rule change
summary: A school district financial dashboard was demonstrated, and feedback was requested. Approvals also included $50,000 for police repairs, contracts for Edgewood Pre-K Academy and police complex lighting, and a workers' compensation settlement. The city also disbanded its ARPA task force, and a resident spoke against the homestead proposal.
decisions: Approved $50,000 transfer for police repairs and maintenance.
Approved $49,745 transfer for parking garage security cameras.
Approved $40,000 transfer for an advisor RFP evaluation fee.
Approved $1,250,000 transfer from the general fund contingency account.
Approved $101,021 appropriation and $7,995 in transfers for road improvements.
Approved the consent agenda except item G.
Approved a letter asking the zoning commission to speed up scheduling for the data center text amendment.
Approved sale of city lots on Rock Road for $6,000, with one no vote.
Disbanded the ARPA task force and sent letters of thanks to its members.
Approved amended Edgewood Pre-K Academy renovation contract, bringing the GMP to $29,873,359.
Authorized the police chief to sign documents for the Connecticut information sharing system.
Approved $92,000 contract amendment for HVAC work at Bill's Community Center, bringing the total to $2,431,829.
Approved LED lighting upgrade at the Bristol Police Complex, 131 North Main Street.
Approved full and final settlement of workers' compensation claims for $136,706.15.
discussion: Financial dashboard: Officials demonstrated a school district financial dashboard and asked for feedback, especially on hard-to-read object codes. Questions were to go through the Board of Finance.

Data center rule timing: Members asked why the zoning commission set the text amendment for January 2027 and said the delay was risky. They noted an Inland Wetlands hearing in December on a Riverside Avenue data center.

Rock Road lot sale: A bidder who offered more than four times the price said he lost to the adjoining owner. Officials said the committee weighed zoning and buildability, and that the city does not have to take the highest bid.
Homestead proposal: A resident said the proposal moves the tax burden to apartment owners and businesses, which would raise rents. The resident asked the state to pay more toward public education.
Chippany golf course: Officials reported over 170 new public golfers in four days and $7,500 in fees. Management proposals are due November 19.
